keyRules: In the open category the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point on the Earth's surface — not simply straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you can count too. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the entity responsible for that obstacle may request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle's height.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or could transfer more than 80 J of kinetic energy on impact) — this applies to toys too. Below 250 g, registration is still mandatory if the drone has a sensor able to capture personal data, unless it is considered a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Training/pilot licence requirements are separate and depend on the drone's class and subcategory.

The minimum age for flying on your own in the open category is 16 — the A1/A3 online training and exam are valid for 5 years and recognised throughout the EU. No age limit: a class C0 drone that is a toy, in subcategory A1, or a privately built drone under 250 g; otherwise younger pilots only under the direct supervision of a pilot who meets the age and training requirements.

Tourists: operator registration and an A1/A3 certificate from another EU/EASA country are also valid in the Czech Republic (you can register in only one country). Outside the EU: register in the first EU/EASA country where you will fly (in the Czech Republic with ÚCL at dron.caa.gov.cz), and if your drone requires training, complete training under EU rules – certificates from non-EU countries are not recognised.
Liability insurance is mandatory in the Czech Republic in subcategory A2 and in A3 for drones over 4 kg (not in A1) — check that your policy covers flights in the Czech Republic.

In airport CTRs and ATZs you may fly without coordination only up to the height set by the grid (check in DroneMap). Higher only after coordination with ŘLP and with the flight marked in DroneMap; in the inner zone of a CTR the flight must always be marked in DroneMap, and above the grid height coordination with the airport operator is also required. Stricter conditions apply at military airports (MCTR). At uncontrolled airports, above the grid height only after coordination with AFIS or the airport operator. Marking in DroneMap does not apply to drones that do not require registration.

In densely populated areas (zone LKR316) the flight area must be marked in advance in DroneMap (dronemap.gov.cz). The marking (here as well as in CTRs and protected nature areas) must include the height, time, type and weight category of the drone, and the operator's registration number. Does not apply to drones for which operator registration is not required.

National parks, protected landscape areas (CHKO) and small-scale protected areas, e.g. nature reserves (zone LKR318): flights only on the basis of prior notification to, or permission from, the competent nature conservation authority, and with the flight area marked in DroneMap. Does not apply to drones for which operator registration is not required.

Roads (zone LKR317): as a rule, within 50 m of the centreline of a motorway or class I road only with the consent of ŘSD; as a rule, within 15 m of the centreline of class II and III roads only with the consent of the road's owner or manager (similarly for local roads outside densely populated areas). The flight area must be marked in DroneMap – does not apply to drones for which operator registration is not required.

In the open category you must keep the drone in direct visual line of sight with the naked eye (glasses/contact lenses are fine; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or bring in an observer to help, with clear and effective communication between you at all times, so that together you can watch the airspace and avoid collisions. “Follow-me” mode is a separate exception only in subcategory A1, permitted within 50 m of the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.

Do not fly under the influence of alcohol or another addictive substance, nor in or near the area of an operation by units of the Integrated Rescue System – both are offences in the Czech Republic (§ 92c of Act No. 49/1997 Coll.). Policie ČR and ÚCL may require you to prove your identity, present your certificate, undergo a preliminary test for addictive substances and interrupt the flight; you must comply with the request.
Night flight is permitted under the EASA open-category baseline when the required green flashing light is used, unless a current geographic zone or national rule imposes a stricter condition.
Fines of up to 3,000,000 CZK (≈ 120,000 €) for violations

Prague: prohibited areas for drones LKP1 PRAŽSKÝ HRAD, LKP329 VLTAVA (the tourist-heavy part of Prague) and LKP330 DEJVICE. In LKP329 and LKP330 you may fly only with a Specific authorisation or a flight authorisation from ÚCL and with the prior consent of Policie ČR (for LKP330, the Military Police); in LKP1 only under the conditions of AIP ENR 5 and ÚCL procedures and with the consent of Policie ČR. Check the boundaries in DroneMap.
importantNotes: In airport CTRs and ATZs, without coordination only up to the height set by the grid (check in DroneMap); higher only after coordination (in a CTR with ŘLP, at uncontrolled airports with AFIS or the airport operator) and with the flight marked in DroneMap; in the inner zone of a CTR, marking is always required

Roads (zone LKR317): for motorways and class I roads, as a rule within 50 m of the centreline only with the consent of ŘSD; for class II and III roads, as a rule within 15 m of the centreline only with the consent of the road's owner or manager
Prague: prohibited areas for drones LKP1 PRAŽSKÝ HRAD, LKP329 VLTAVA and LKP330 DEJVICE – flights only with ÚCL permission and police consent
The GDPR applies to the collection of identifiable images
